slides.headline: ONE ARTIST FROM THE PHILIPPINES JUST TOOK ON AN ENTIRE AI MEME COMPANY
AN AI APP SELLS HIS MEME AS PAID ADS
slides.body: The 'Running Away Balloon' meme by Filipino artist Superelmer went viral in 2017. A company called Memes Apps now charges businesses for an AI tool that copies his comic into ad templates. Nobody asked Saflor. Nobody paid him

slides.headline: A COURT RULED MEMES CAN'T GO IN ADS
slides.body: In 2024, a judge ruled in the 'SuccessKid' meme case that using a meme in a campaign ad without the creator's ok is not fair use. Internet law expert Eric Goldman says Saflor started 'on the right foot' and is telling 'the right story for the judge'

slides.headline: HE SUED THE APP, NOT THE ADVERTISERS
slides.body: Internet law expert Eric Goldman called this move 'gutsy' and a legal first. Saflor went straight for the tool selling his work, not the companies buying it. Goldman warns the court will 'check more cautiously' because a ruling here touches every meme app online

slides.headline: YOUR MEME ADS JUST PUT YOU AT RISK
slides.body: After the 2024 SuccessKid ruling, using a meme in your ads without the artist's ok is officially not fair use. That case was about one campaign ad, and the artist still won. One AI-powered content audit scans your entire library in minutes, no legal team needed

caption:
Swipe to see why the artist behind one of the internet's biggest memes just sued an AI company for selling his work 👆

The 'Running Away Balloon' meme by Filipino artist Superelmer went viral in 2017, a company called Memes Apps now charges businesses for an AI tool that copies his comic into ad templates, Saflor sued them this month after nobody asked or paid him, a 2024 'SuccessKid' ruling already said memes can't go in ads without permission, internet law expert Eric Goldman called the legal strategy 'gutsy' and said the artist is telling 'the right story for the judge,' but warned a win could change the rules for every meme app on the internet

AI tools are quietly grabbing art people made and selling it to businesses. This lawsuit could set the rules for all of them. If the court sides with the artist, every company using memes without permission gets a problem.
